purpose: Structured CFPB Cash App fraud-process enforcement ledger linking reported consumer loss, dispute-control failure, formal correction, and ordered redress while preserving individual receipt, recovery, trust, and exit as open.

events.geography: United States; Block Inc. and Cash App users
events.date_precision: CFPB enforcement action dated January 16, 2025; underlying user incidents and account freezes span an unreported period
events.denominator: Consumers and fraud-related disputes described in the CFPB enforcement action; no population incidence or individual redress denominator is retained
events.method: Structured extraction from the official CFPB enforcement action and case/payment-status recheck
events.missingness: No completed redress-plan report, affected-consumer list, per-person refund amount, transaction date, disputed amount by person, investigation timeline, payment date, receipt confirmation, remaining loss, account correction, or later behavior is retained; the order's class definitions and aggregate 153,866-claim count do not identify a stable account
events.exposure: The CFPB reported that Block's dispute-investigation and security practices exposed Cash App users to fraud risk and that some reported fraud was not handled through required investigation processes
events.alternatives_before_action: Users could seek Block dispute review, other payment-provider or banking routes, law-enforcement help, private recovery, or stop using the service; actual feasible alternatives and switching are not observed
events.immediate_burden_or_benefit: Fraud loss and dispute-control dependence could impose money, time, documentation, and access burdens; the order identifies at least 153,866 unauthorized-transfer claims without required timely provisional credit when investigations exceeded 10 business days, but does not quantify each consumer's burden
events.choice_or_response: Users reported or disputed losses and Block operated the investigation process; the CFPB's current case page says consumers do not need to take action at this time to obtain redress, while publishing a phone, email, and mail route for redress inquiries. Individual repeat contact, abandonment, or channel switching is not retained
events.person_or_actor_with_control: Block controlled account security and dispute investigation; CFPB controlled enforcement; users had limited control over correction after a reported loss
events.remedy_or_institutional_response: The CFPB ordered operational changes, a separate $55 million civil penalty, and at least $75 million and up to $120 million in consumer redress; the order defines a frozen-account affected class as an account frozen at least 14 days with a balance of at least $25, assigns that class a $50 redress component, and requires a redress plan plus post-plan report identifying consumers/accounts receiving redress and total amount paid. The current case page says consumers do not need to take action at this time and provides a direct redress contact route
events.immediate_outcome: Formal enforcement and a defined consumer-redress obligation are documented
events.protected_outcome: Operational changes and redress may protect or compensate some users, but no individual account correction or payment is verified
events.sacrificed_outcome: Unrecovered loss, effort, access, and trust costs for affected users cannot be identified from the public case record
events.cost_risk_transfer: Weak dispute controls can shift fraud and correction risk from the payment platform to users; the enforcement order redistributes some prospective and financial responsibility back toward the firm
events.later_outcome: A 2026-10-19 recheck found Block/Cash App absent from the CFPB ongoing and closed payment-by-case lists; the list page was last modified October 15, 2026. The Block case page still provides a redress contact route, but no completed recipient-level report is retained; individual eligibility, payment, receipt, residual loss, continued use, switching, trust, and exit remain open
events.meaning_and_attribution: The agency attributes process failures to Block, but user-level fairness, blame, legitimacy, and trust change are not measured
events.public_or_collective_response: Enforcement is observed; user organizing, complaint persistence, political action, and collective response are not linked
events.counterexample: A redress pool, an order requiring a final affected-consumer list, and a payment-reporting requirement do not prove that every affected user was identified, paid, made whole, or able to leave
events.source_and_uncertainty: Official CFPB enforcement record and Block consent order (https://files.consumerfinance.gov/f/documents/cfpb_block-inc-consent-order_2025-01.pdf); CFPB payments-by-case page rechecked 2026-10-19 (page last modified October 15, 2026) with no Block/Cash App entry visible, and the current Block case page provides a redress contact route while saying consumers do not need to take action at this time. The non-listing is not proof of nonpayment; the post-plan reporting requirement remains a measurement contract, not a completed recipient-level recovery study

arrows.evidence: The CFPB enforcement record describes fraud exposure and failures to handle some reported fraud through required investigations
arrows.counterexample: The enforcement record is not a population incidence estimate and does not identify every affected user
arrows.remaining_gap: User-level transaction, dispute, amount, timing, and investigation records

arrows.evidence: The CFPB issued an enforcement action requiring fraud-handling and security-practice changes
arrows.counterexample: An ordered process change does not establish implementation quality or user-level correction
arrows.remaining_gap: Implementation audit, user account correction, recurrence, and accessible override route

arrows.evidence: The order requires at least $75 million and up to $120 million in consumer redress, a separate $55 million civil penalty, and a post-plan report identifying consumers/accounts receiving redress and total amount paid
arrows.counterexample: An ordered pool is not an issued payment, recipient receipt, or adequate recovery
arrows.remaining_gap: Eligibility, distribution route, payment date, amount, receipt, and remaining loss

arrows.to: individual financial recovery and restored account control
arrows.evidence: The public case and payment-status recheck do not expose a user-level distribution or receipt record
arrows.counterexample: The absence of a public listing does not prove that no payment or company-administered distribution has occurred
arrows.remaining_gap: Privacy-approved account/payment follow-up with receipt, adequacy, correction time, and residual loss

arrows.to: continued use, switching, trust, or exit
arrows.evidence: No user-level later-use, alternative-provider, trust, or exit outcome is linked to the enforcement record
arrows.counterexample: Continued use can reflect dependence or convenience, while non-use can reflect friction or inability to switch
arrows.remaining_gap: Same-user follow-up on account access, alternatives, repeat effort, trust, switching, and exit reason

boundary: This ledger establishes a formal consumer-protection and redress stage. It does not estimate Cash App user harm, payment receipt, recovery, trust change, or exit.
storage_boundary: No user-level account, payment, or transaction file is retained; the ledger contains only bounded official enforcement facts, the public distribution-status boundary, and explicit open links.
